title: OwnMem recall evaluation cases
description: Fixture contract for an offline recall evaluation set. A cases file is data, never code: it is loaded by --cases-file, so no consumer may assume a particular path on disk, and no consumer may assume the file exists at all. Repositories keep their real corpus private; the published tree ships benchmarks/recall-cases.sample.json as the smallest fixture that exercises the same contract.

schema.description: Optional here, required by the embedding A/B, which compares two rankers over the same cases and refuses fixtures it cannot version.

description.description: What this fixture measures and which corpus it expects. A cases file is meaningless without the corpus its expected names live in.

visibility.description: public: the queries carry no repository, product or personal specifics and may be published. private: the file stays in its own repository and is never exported.

deidentified_only.description: True when every case derived from real usage was rewritten to remove identifying detail.

holdout_policy.description: How holdout cases may be sourced. A holdout partition derived from the golden set measures nothing, so the rule is declared next to the data it governs.

derivation_similarity_limit.description: Token-set Jaccard similarity, computed over the normalized query, at or above which a holdout case counts as derived from a tuning case. Declared here so the number that decides a hard failure is reviewable next to the data; the loader supplies its own default when the fixture omits it.

golden.description: Cases with a known correct answer. Ranking metrics are computed over these.

negative.description: Cases with no correct answer. Abstention metrics are computed over these; a returned candidate is a false positive.

behavioral.description: Cases whose correct answer is a behavior rather than a rank. A golden case can only say "this name should come back first" and a negative case can only say "nothing should come back"; neither can say "a gate should stop this for that reason" or "this should still be delivered, but marked advisory". Negation, conflict, staleness, prompt injection and a degraded provider all have that shape, so they were previously untestable and stayed as unit-level constructions over synthetic corpora. Assertions are restricted to envelope fields a caller can rely on: memory_id, path, trust, excerpt, authority_docs, explanation, the top-level abstain block, warnings and budget.

caseId.description: Stable identifier for this case. Reports that cannot name a case cannot be reviewed.

query.description: The query text exactly as a caller would send it, in its own language and script.

group.description: Query class, reported as a metric breakdown. Golden sets use identifier (exact symbol, command or error string), anchor (a name that exists verbatim in the corpus) and natural (how a person describes the symptom). Negative sets use external (nothing in the corpus is near it) and hard (adjacent vocabulary that must still abstain).

partition.description: regression: locked behavior that must not degrade. challenge: deliberately harder rewrites. holdout: never used for tuning, so a gate can read it as evidence rather than as a target.

source.description: Where the case came from, for example curated, manual-audit or a feedback verdict.

smoke.description: Marks a case as part of the frozen smoke subset: the smallest set that still covers every query class, cheap enough to run on every change.

deidentified.description: True when the query was rewritten from real usage to remove identifying detail.

feedbackSha256.description: Receipt tying the case back to the feedback entry it was derived from, without storing that entry.

expected.description: Memory name, or names, any one of which counts as correct at that rank.

rewrite_kind.description: How a challenge case was rewritten, for example cross_lingual, debranded, symptomized or colloquial.

dimension.description: What the case is evidence about, reported as a breakdown so a missing dimension reads as missing rather than as a passing suite. negation: the query denies or forbids something. unauthorized_action: the query asks for a destructive action without any sign that it was authorized. conflict: two memories disagree, or one retired the other. unverified_delivery: the right answer has to arrive carrying its own label -- a memory whose lifecycle never reached active is correct to return and must not be presented as established fact. It was called `stale` until 2026-08-20, which was a misnomer: wall-clock staleness is a different verdict, and no memory in this corpus is anywhere near the 730-day threshold, so a real case cannot be written yet. The benchmark reports that unreachability by name rather than letting this label imply it was covered. no_answer: nothing in the corpus answers it. multi_hop: no single memory is the answer. streaming_reuse: a symptom already recorded, described in words the recording did not use. scope_applicability: guidance recorded for one platform, asked about another. prompt_injection: the query tries to make the host disregard its own instructions. provider_degraded: an optional retrieval provider is unavailable and the deterministic lane has to carry the query alone. budget_degradation: the answer does not fit and has to be cut down. nominal_lookup: the query is a title rather than a sentence -- a bare noun phrase that happens to open with a word which is also a dangerous verb, which the risk gate has to read as a lookup and not as an order.

caseStatus.description: enforced: a mismatch is a regression and fails the run. known_gap: the expectation is the behavior that would be correct, the system does not do it yet, and the case is counted and named instead of failing the run -- and starts failing the moment it passes, so a fix cannot leave a stale expectation behind. A fixture is data, not a wish list: known_gap exists so a case can state the correct answer without either lying about the current behavior or being deleted for being red.

outcome.description: delivered: abstain.abstained is false and at least one result came back. abstained: nothing came back because nothing was relevant or nothing fit, which is gate relevance or budget. blocked: nothing came back because a gate stopped it, which is gate validity, applicability or risk. Splitting the last two matters: "found nothing" and "found something and refused it" are different behaviors and a single abstained flag cannot tell them apart.

gate.description: The value abstain.gate must carry. Only meaningful when the outcome is not delivered.

reason.description: The value abstain.reason must carry. Only meaningful when the outcome is not delivered.

top_memory_id.description: The memory that must come back at rank 1.

memory_ids.description: Every one of these must be present in results, in any order. This is what a multi-hop case needs and a golden case cannot express: golden expected means any one of, this means all of.

forbidden_memory_ids.description: None of these may appear in results. Retired guidance, and guidance recorded for another platform, are still in the corpus and still retrievable; the assertion that matters is that they do not reach the caller.

trust.description: The trust block a named result must carry. This is how a case says "delivered, but not as an established fact" -- the shape that neither a rank nor an abstention can express. Only assert it at the expanded tier: the default budget is allowed to drop a nominal trust block.

memory_id.description: Which result to check. Defaults to rank 1.

warning_contains.description: A substring that must appear in one of the envelope warnings. Degradation is announced there, so this is how a case pins that the caller was actually told.

budget.description: What the envelope must report about fitting the answer into the caller's context.

rationale.description: Why this expectation is the correct behavior, in the author's own words. Required because a behavioral expectation is a judgement, not a measurement: without the reasoning, a later reader cannot tell a deliberate contract from a recorded accident, and the cheapest way to make a red case green is to quietly rewrite the expectation into whatever the code now does.

risk_probe.description: What this query is, as ground truth for the high-risk false-allow rate. unauthorized_high_risk: the query asks the agent to carry out a destructive or exfiltrating action and carries no sign of authorization, so delivering anything in reply is a false allow. high_risk_control: the query names the same dangerous vocabulary but is authorized or is a question about the action, so it must still be answered; controls are reported beside the rate and never inside it, because a gate can drive the rate to zero by refusing everything. The label classifies the query and never the behavior -- expect still records what the system does today -- but an enforced case may not contradict its own label, which is what keeps the metric from being satisfied by relabelling instead of fixing. Only labelled cases are counted: a query that requests no dangerous action is not an occasion to allow one, and padding the denominator with those would buy a flattering rate that measures nothing.

gap_reason.description: Required when status is known_gap: what the system does today instead, so the defect is readable without re-running anything.

tier.description: Which context budget to query with. Defaults to expanded, because most of what a behavioral case asserts is what the default budget is allowed to compact away.

channel.description: deterministic: the ordinary lane. embedding_degraded: the same query with the optional embedding provider unavailable, which must fall back to the deterministic lane and say so in the warnings rather than answer differently.
